task.text:
WRITING TASK 2
You should spend about 40 minutes on this task.
Some people say history is one of the most important school subjects. Other people think that, in today’s world, subjects like science and technology are more important than history. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.
Write at least 250 words.

paragraphs: Nowadays, some might argue that history is one of the most important school subjects. Other people argue that science and technology are more important than history. Personally, I agree with the first school of thought.

Admittedly, science and technology is very important in life now. Initially, Internet, AI and robot is develop dramatically, so that, students in schools need to learn how to control a robot or AI, because if they don't know this knowledge in the future it is very hard for to they looking for a good career which demand people need a good skill to control robot. Furthermore, in right now, AI can help students to do their homework, if you have a question, or a lesson, which you don't understand, you ask AI such as Gemini or Chat GPT, they will give you a answer very fastly. Finally, students in schools study science and technology well, can show for their teachers the depth of thought and have a good performance in class or school.

However, I agree with idea that history is as important as science or technology. There are many reasons for I think that. Firstly, after a long day in school with many many subjects, which demand students need logic, history is a simple subject, which can tell to students many stories in the past, is the best way for students relax, but they also have more knowledge. Secondly, History can teach students about WW1 or WW2 and many terrible war in the past, so that they can know how to respect anythings they have right now. As a result, students can find their motivation for their life and love their country more.

Finally, I always believe that history is one the most important school subjects. More over, history is as important as science and technology. Because history can teach students about social life and have many big benefits, history is one of the best subjects in schools in the past, right now or in the future.
review.overall: Em đã dành đoạn riêng cho hai quan điểm và giữ ý kiến rằng lịch sử xứng đáng được coi trọng cùng khoa học, công nghệ. Cấu trúc Admittedly rồi However giúp người đọc nhận ra em đang thừa nhận lợi ích của nhóm môn kia trước khi trình bày lập trường. Tuy nhiên, ví dụ dùng công cụ trả lời bài tập chưa giải thích vì sao học khoa học và công nghệ quan trọng hơn; đoạn lịch sử cũng cần nói rõ việc học chiến tranh dẫn tới hiểu biết hoặc thái độ nào. Em hãy tập viết câu ngắn, đủ chủ ngữ và động từ, rồi nối các bước lý giải thay vì ghép nhiều ý bằng dấu phẩy.

criteria.label: Task Response
criteria.comment: Cả hai quan điểm được trình bày và lập trường coi lịch sử rất quan trọng vẫn rõ, dù em cũng xem khoa học/công nghệ có giá trị. Ý về kỹ năng công nghệ và bài học lịch sử có liên quan, nhưng ví dụ dùng công cụ làm bài tập, môn lịch sử giúp thư giãn và lòng biết ơn còn thiếu các bước giải thích để hỗ trợ kết luận.

criteria.label: Coherence and Cohesion
criteria.comment: Bốn đoạn và các bước Admittedly–However–Finally tạo hướng đi có thể theo dõi. Trong đoạn công nghệ, nhiều vế nối bằng dấu phẩy khiến ý nghề nghiệp, công cụ hỗ trợ học và kết quả ở lớp chưa được nối theo một chuỗi rõ ràng.

criteria.label: Lexical Resource
criteria.comment: Em có từ đúng chủ đề như career, technology, history, respect và motivation nhưng lặp nhiều từ chung như important, good, many. Fastly, anythings, a answer và một số cụm như depth of thought thiếu chính xác.

criteria.label: Grammatical Range and Accuracy
criteria.comment: Em thử nhiều mệnh đề nguyên nhân và điều kiện, song đa số câu dài có lỗi hòa hợp, dạng động từ hoặc dấu câu: science and technology is, is develop, for to they looking, students relax. Câu ngắn đúng chưa xuất hiện thường xuyên để giữ nghĩa các câu dài ổn định.

annotations.replacement: history remains valuable for understanding society, alongside the practical skills taught through science and technology

paragraphs.text: Some people regard history as a central part of school education, whereas others would give greater priority to science and technology in the modern world. I believe history deserves to remain one of the important subjects in schools, even though the scientific subjects also teach skills that students need. Both areas contribute to a complete education in different ways.

Admittedly, science and technology are valuable because many people now use digital systems at work and in daily life. Students who learn how such systems operate can do more than receive an answer from a device: they can test information, solve practical problems and decide whether a result is reliable. For example, a class project might ask students to collect data about energy use and compare possible ways to reduce it. This would develop their ability to work with evidence, a skill that could also help them in further study or in a technical career. These benefits explain why schools should give science and technology serious attention.

However, history can be just as valuable for a different reason. Accounts of earlier people and events can engage students while helping them understand how their society developed. Learning about the First and Second World Wars, for instance, may help them recognise the costs of conflict and value the peace they experience today. A history lesson can also invite students to consider why people made certain decisions and how those choices affected later generations. This is more useful than simply memorising dates: it gives young people a way to think about their country and their responsibilities within it.

In conclusion, I consider history one of the most important school subjects because it develops understanding of the past and of society. Science and technology deserve attention as well because they build practical skills. Schools should provide opportunities to study both, rather than assuming that one area alone can meet every educational need.
